security_level_rationale: RCP operates in a safety-critical in-vehicle network. SL-2 provides protection against intentional violation using simple means with low motivation and resources (e.g., insider attack or opportunistic compromise of a connected ECU).

threats.description: Attacker forges zone-controller identity to inject commands
Attacker flips bits in transit to cause erroneous actuation

threats.residual_risk: medium — REQ-SEQENF-003's rx_enforce_seq monotonic-sequence check is additive standalone plumbing (crate::request::evaluate_rx_enforce_seq), not yet wired into a live request-acceptance path, since Milestone 9's e2e REPLACE cutover removed the legacy ReplayGuard sliding-window mechanism with no live replacement built yet

threats.description: Attacker floods RCP with low-priority commands to delay critical ones
Attacker crafts oversized payload to overflow allocator
threats.residual_risk: negligible — REQ-WIRE-007's NTSCF envelope size limit is live and dispatch-wired (crate::mock::RcServer's own decode path); REQ-CAN-005's CanDataFrame::decode payload-ceiling check retargets the retired REQ-CANBR-004 (Milestone 9's canbr REPLACE cutover deleted the old Zone/Command-coupled CanBridge check with no direct analog) but, like the rest of crate::can, is additive standalone plumbing not yet wired into a live decode/dispatch path

threats.description: Attacker monitors command bus to extract vehicle state
